 =\sum_{u\in\Omega_I}\widetilde r(u)(\pi_I)_\#q_D^s(u)
 =\sum_{u\in\Omega_I}\widetilde r(u)(\pi_I)_\#q_D^\star(u)
 =rq_D^\star,
\]
so the row transports.  Conversely, if \(r\) is not constant on a fiber, choose \(\omega_0,\omega_1\) in that fiber with different row values.  The laws \(\delta_{\omega_0}\) and \(\delta_{\omega_1}\) have the same \(\pi_I\)-marginal but different \(r\)-expectations, giving a two-point leakage certificate.  Testing all pairs of profiles with equal \(\pi_I\) is finite.  This proves both necessity and sufficiency under \((\mathrm{KMI})\), while also showing why \((\mathrm{KMI})\), which is absent from the frozen core, cannot be inferred from the graph alone.

statements.statement:
There are two exact finite frontiers with different scopes.

First, assume \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\). Then \(\Theta(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and, for every finite collection \(\mathcal F\) of declared target-domain counterfactual cells,
\[
\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\}
=
\{(\Psi_C^\star(\theta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
Every \(\Psi_C^s\) is multi-affine in the district response-law blocks and has total degree at most the number of districts visited by \(C\). Every point of the right-hand range is realized by a district-saturated SCM family on the original observed alphabets \(\mathcal X\).

Second, for an arbitrary acyclic directed mixed graph, if \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\), then \(\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and
\[
\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\}
=
\{(\Phi_{C,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\vartheta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):
\vartheta\in\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
The canonical realization also uses the original observed alphabets and retains the internal latent-factor restrictions of \(G\).

For either exact row
\[
(\mathfrak C,\Lambda,\Xi)
\in
\{(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P),\Theta(\mathcal P),\Psi),
(\mathcal C(\mathcal P),\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P),\Phi_{\mathrm{can}})\},
\]
provided \(\mathfrak C\ne\varnothing\), the quantities
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star)
\]
are respectively the attained sharp lower and upper bounds for the target cell. At least one bound is strictly inside the logical interval \([0,1]\) exactly when the lower endpoint is positive or the upper endpoint is less than one, and the cell is identified exactly when the two extrema agree. If the extrema differ, minimizing and maximizing realizations give two original-alphabet same-menu SCM families attaining different endpoint values. No assertion is made that every scalar value between the two extrema is attained. These are finite semialgebraic characterizations.

For the same row let
\[
e_-(\Lambda)=\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star),
\qquad e_+(\Lambda)=\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star).
\]
If \(e_+(\Lambda)=0\), evidence is zero throughout \(\mathfrak C\); if \(e_-(\Lambda)=0<e_+(\Lambda)\), positivity is not uniform. In either case a conditional functional on all of \(\mathfrak C\) is rejected before division. If \(e_-(\Lambda)>0\), the quantities
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\]
are the attained sharp lower and upper conditional bounds. If they differ, their endpoint models are distinct; no interval-filling property of the conditional image is asserted. Under this positivity condition, \(Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\) throughout \(\mathfrak C\) if and only if
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}
\{\Xi_{B_\sigma\cap E}^\star(x^\star)-\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)\}>0,
\]
and opposite strict rankings occur in two same-menu original-alphabet models if and only if the minimum of the displayed gap is negative and its maximum is positive. Thus this strict minimum is the exact safe-pruning certificate for the chosen fiber.

Finally, for every district \(D\),
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)\subseteq\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
If \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds, the one-district fiber-projection theorem gives the exact local equality
\[
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)=\mathcal K_D(m_D),
\]
and \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) itself entails a nonempty focal-district-saturated compatibility fiber. This equality requires saturation only of the focal district and preserves the graph-compatible restrictions of every \(D'\ne D\). Cross-district coupling of a complete supplied cell is harmless for the fixed-baseline replacement exactly when its baseline-averaged focal row lies in \(R_D(m_D)\), because
\[
R_D(m_D)=\operatorname{span}\{q-q':q,q'\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\}^{\perp}.
\]
Nonemptiness of \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\) together with \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\), and hence with \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\), is a baseline-free sufficient certificate for this equality. The baseline-averaged predicate is generally baseline-dependent and not directly checkable from menu cells alone; allowing a different baseline for each candidate \(q\) is not asserted. Outside focal-district saturation and baseline-averaged separation, \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\) is certified only as an outer relaxation. This local equality is distinct from the first, all-district-saturated global row, whose Cartesian district variation makes the multi-affine program exact. Consequently a failed local face test is not a global nonidentification certificate outside the focal projection theorem's scope; distinct endpoint optimizers of the appropriate exact global program are the paired-model certificate whenever their objective values differ.
statements.justification: The theorem separates exact all-district multi-affine variation, exact sparse canonical optimization, and exact single-baseline focal-district geometry.
statements.gap: Global programs retain every cross-district polynomial equality; locally, a weaker baseline-averaged condition preserves those cells than pointwise active-slice control.
statements.consumer: Global bounds and pruning use exact endpoint optimizers, while local LP certificates use focal saturation plus baseline-averaged separation or its baseline-free sufficient checks.
statements.proof_tex:
We prove the two exact finite range equalities separately and then derive their optimization consequences.

Assume first \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\) and take \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\).  For every domain \(s\) and district \(D\), push the law of \(U_D^s\in\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\) forward to the finite profile coordinates \(\Omega_D\) visited by the declared menus and target cells; call it \(q_D^s\).  District factorization makes the joint profile law the product of these district laws.  Finite recursive evaluation and total probability therefore give, for every declared cell \(C\),
\[
P_{M^s}(C)
=\sum_{\omega\in\prod_D\Omega_D}
\mathbf 1\{C\text{ is true under recursive evaluation of }\omega\}
\prod_Dq_D^s(\omega_D)
=\Psi_C^s(\theta^s).
\tag{1}
\]
If \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), district-kernel invariance gives \(q_D^s=q_D^\star\).  Typed-menu realizability and (1) give
\(\Psi_{C_{a,v}}^s(\theta^s)=P_a^s(v)\) for every complete supplied cell.  Thus \(\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)\), which proves the forward saturated range inclusion simultaneously for all cells in \(\mathcal F\).

Conversely, take \(\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)\).  Because each declared alphabet is finite and nonempty, complete each \(\omega_D\in\Omega_D\) deterministically at unvisited parent configurations, obtaining an injection \(\iota_D:\Omega_D\to\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\).  Push \(q_D^s\) through \(\iota_D\), take distinct district blocks independently, and let each structural equation read its component response map.  Acyclicity gives unique recursive evaluation in \(\mathcal X\).  The unrestricted response-block clause of \(\mathrm{def:district\text{-}saturated\text{-}model\text{-}class}\) admits these laws, and using the same \(\iota_D\) across domains preserves every unchanged-district equality.  The complete-cell equations defining \(\Theta(\mathcal P)\) yield
\[
P_{M_\theta^s}^a(v)=\Psi_{C_{a,v}}^s(\theta^s)=P_a^s(v).
\]
Hence \(\mathbf M_\theta\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\), it uses the original alphabets, and it realizes every corresponding \(\Psi\)-value.  This proves the reverse saturated range inclusion.

For the arbitrary-ADMG row, take \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\).  Recursive compatibility permits application of \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}canonical\text{-}counterfactual\text{-}equivalence}\) in every domain to the finite joint collection containing all response-map counterfactuals used by the supplied and target cells.  The resulting graph-compatible canonical SCM uses the same observed alphabets and preserves their joint counterfactual law.  In particular it preserves every district response-profile law, so district-kernel invariance implies
\[
q_{D,\mathrm{can}}^s(\cdot;\vartheta^s)
=q_{D,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\cdot;\vartheta^\star)
\quad\text{when }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing.
\]
Preservation of each complete supplied cell gives
\(\Phi_{C_{a,v},\mathrm{can}}^s(\vartheta^s)=P_a^s(v)\).  Thus \(\vartheta\in\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\), and preservation of \(\mathcal F\) proves the forward canonical inclusion.

Conversely, \(\vartheta\in\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\) consists of graph-compatible one-hot structural tables and finite canonical exogenous probability vectors.  The one-hot constraints choose exactly one value in \(\mathcal X_V\) at every structural input, the simplex constraints define probability laws, and the graph-compatible latent restrictions and product law across districts give recursive compatibility and district factorization.  Its response-law equalities give district-kernel invariance; district closure is fixed by the model-class instance; and the complete supplied-cell equations give each entire supplied law.  Hence its canonical realization lies in \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), uses the original alphabets, and realizes the displayed \(\Phi_{\mathrm{can}}\)-values.  This proves the reverse canonical inclusion.

Both parameter fibers are finite-dimensional and bounded.  The saturated fiber is a closed subset of a finite product of simplices cut out by finitely many polynomial equalities.  The graph-compatible canonical fiber is a closed subset of a finite union of products of simplices and finite one-hot sets cut out by finitely many polynomial equalities and inequalities.  Thus both are compact semialgebraic sets; nonemptiness follows from the corresponding assumed SCM fiber and forward inclusion.  Each summand in (1) contains at most one coordinate from each visited district, so \(\Psi_C^s\) is multi-affine and has total degree at most the number of visited districts.

Fix either exact range row \((\mathfrak C,\Lambda,\Xi)\) and a target cell \(T\).  The continuous target polynomial attains its minimum and maximum on the nonempty compact fiber.  Exact range equality makes these the attained sharp SCM bounds.  Since cell probabilities lie in \([0,1]\), at least one endpoint is strictly inside the logical interval exactly when the lower endpoint is positive or the upper endpoint is less than one.  Identification is equivalent to equality of the extrema.  If they differ, attaining minimizers and maximizers give original-alphabet same-menu SCMs with unequal endpoint values; no claim about intermediate values is needed.

The nonnegative evidence polynomial likewise attains its extrema.  If its maximum is zero, evidence is zero throughout the fiber.  If its minimum is zero and maximum positive, a compatible minimizing model has zero evidence, so positivity is not uniform.  In both cases a conditional functional on the whole fiber is rejected before division.  If the evidence minimum is positive, the ratio
\[
x\longmapsto
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\]
is continuous on the compact fiber and attains its sharp lower and upper bounds.  Exact range equality supplies endpoint SCMs, and unequal extrema supply distinct same-menu models.

For two arms the evidence denominator is common and strictly positive.  Therefore
\[
Q_\sigma^\star(\mathbf M_x)-Q_\rho^\star(\mathbf M_x)
=\frac{\Xi_{B_\sigma\cap E}^\star(x^\star)
-\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}
{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\]
has the sign of its numerator.  A continuous numerator-gap polynomial is positive everywhere on a compact fiber exactly when its attained minimum is positive.  Its negative minimum and positive maximum are attained by two same-menu original-alphabet models with opposite rankings, and conversely such a pair forces those endpoint signs.  This proves the exact pruning claim.

Finally, the broad part of \(\mathrm{thm:one\text{-}district\text{-}fiber\text{-}projection}\) gives \(\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)\subseteq\mathcal K_D(m_D)\).  Under \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\), its exact part gives
\[
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)=\mathcal K_D(m_D),
\qquad
R_D(m_D)=\operatorname{span}\{q-q':q,q'\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\}^\perp.
\tag{2}
\]
That predicate already supplies one baseline \(\mathbf M^0\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\).  Holding its nonfocal laws fixed, the probability change of an admissible complete cell under \(q_0\mapsto q\) is exactly
\[
\bar\chi_{C_{a,v}}^{s,\mathbf M^0}(q-q_0)=0,
\]
where zero follows from (2) and the defining membership of the averaged row in \(R_D(m_D)\).  This proves why baseline-averaged rather than pointwise slice membership is the exact condition for this fixed-baseline construction.  The hierarchy lemma shows that nonemptiness plus \(\mathsf{ASep}_D\), and therefore nonemptiness plus \(\mathsf{Sep}_D\), is sufficient.  Its strict example shows that the baseline-averaged condition can apply even when individual Boolean slices are outside the active row space.

The focal construction changes only the response block at \(D\) and its unchanged-source copies, retaining every nonfocal graph-compatible restriction.  The first exact global row instead saturates every district so that its full Cartesian multi-affine fiber is exact.  Without focal-district saturation and the single-baseline averaged condition, the local face is only an outer relaxation; allowing a baseline to vary with \(q\) would merely restate projection membership and is not used.  Distinct endpoint optimizers of the appropriate exact global program remain the required original-alphabet paired-model certificate.

statements.statement:
For every district \(D\),
\[
\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\Longrightarrow\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P).
\]
The implication is strict in general.  In particular, take two independent binary response coordinates \(Y_0\) and \(Z\) generated by distinct singleton districts, let \(D\) be the district generating \(Y_0\), and supply in the target domain both the complete marginal law of \(Y_0\) and the complete joint law of \((Y_0,Z)\).  The resulting menu satisfies \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) but not \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\).
statements.proof_tex:
Assume \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\), and fix a transport-admissible complete supplied cell \(C\) and a nonfocal profile \(\omega_{-D}\).  By \(\mathrm{def:district\text{-}separated\text{-}menu}\), at least one of the two permitted structural cases applies.  If the recursive indicator of \(C\) is independent of \(\omega_D\), then its fixed-\(\omega_{-D}\) slice is either the zero row or \(\mathbf 1^\top\).  The zero row belongs to every row space, and \(\mathbf 1^\top\in\operatorname{row}(A_D)\) because \(\mathrm{def:stacked\text{-}menu\text{-}system}\) prepends the normalization row.  Hence the slice lies in \(R_D(m_D)\).

If instead the indicator depends only on \(\omega_D\), \(\mathrm{def:district\text{-}separated\text{-}menu}\) requires its raw row to occur in \(A_D\).  Every fixed-\(\omega_{-D}\) slice is that raw row, so it belongs to \(\operatorname{row}(A_D)\subseteq R_D(m_D)\).  These cases cover every admissible cell and every nonfocal profile, proving \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\).

For strictness, consider two binary response coordinates \(Y_0\) and \(Z\) generated by independent singleton district blocks, and put \(D=D_{Y_0}\).  For \(y,z\in\{0,1\}\), define
\[
h_y(\omega_D)=\mathbf 1\{Y_0(\omega_D)=y\},
\qquad
k_z(\omega_{-D})=\mathbf 1\{Z(\omega_{-D})=z\}.
\]
Supplying the complete marginal law of \(Y_0\) retains both rows \(h_0,h_1\) in \(A_D\).  The complete joint cell \(\{Y_0=y,Z=z\}\) has the genuine cross-district indicator
\[
h_y(\omega_D)k_z(\omega_{-D}).
\]
Because the binary profile sets contain profiles producing both values, this indicator is neither independent of \(\omega_D\) nor a function of \(\omega_D\) alone.  Thus \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\) fails.  On fixing \(\omega_{-D}\), however, its focal slice is \(0\) when \(k_z(\omega_{-D})=0\) and is \(h_y\) when \(k_z(\omega_{-D})=1\).  Both rows belong to \(\operatorname{row}(A_D)\).  The marginal cells have slices \(h_y\), and the same argument applies to every joint cell.  Therefore every required slice belongs to \(R_D(m_D)\), so \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds.  Independent Bernoulli laws on the two finite singleton response blocks realize the supplied marginal and joint laws on the declared binary alphabets, completing the promised strict example.

statements.statement:
For every district \(D\),
\[
\bigl\{\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing
\text{ and }\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\bigr\}
\Longrightarrow \mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P).
\]
Together with \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\Longrightarrow\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\), this gives the convenient hierarchy
\[
\bigl\{\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing
\text{ and }\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\bigr\}
\Longrightarrow
\bigl\{\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing
\text{ and }\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\bigr\}
\Longrightarrow \mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P).
\]
The second implication is strict on finite original alphabets: there is a three-vertex binary DAG and a complete target-domain menu for which \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds but \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) fails because two Boolean focal slices outside \(R_D(m_D)\) average to a row inside it under the witnessing nonfocal product law.
statements.justification: This hierarchy makes the sharp single-baseline preservation premise explicit while retaining two increasingly simple sufficient checks.
statements.gap: Pointwise active-slice control is stronger than the fixed-baseline construction needs because only averages under the frozen nonfocal product law enter complete-cell probabilities.
statements.consumer: The focal projection theorem and its identification, dominance, frontier, and global corollaries use baseline-averaged separation for exact lifting.
statements.proof_tex:
Assume first that \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\) and \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\).  Choose any \(\mathbf M^0\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\).  By \(\mathrm{ass:district\text{-}factorization}\), for each domain \(s\) the nonfocal response profiles have the product probability law \(\nu_{-D}^{0,s}\) in \(\mathrm{def:baseline\text{-}averaged\text{-}active\text{-}slice\text{-}menu}\).  For every transport-admissible complete supplied cell and every \(\omega_{-D}\), \(\mathrm{def:active\text{-}slice\text{-}separated\text{-}menu}\) gives
\[
\chi_{C_{a,v},\omega_{-D}}\in R_D(m_D).
\]
Because \(R_D(m_D)\) is a linear subspace and the sum defining \(\bar\chi_{C_{a,v}}^{s,\mathbf M^0}\) is finite,
\[
\bar\chi_{C_{a,v}}^{s,\mathbf M^0}
=\sum_{\omega_{-D}}\nu_{-D}^{0,s}(\omega_{-D})
\chi_{C_{a,v},\omega_{-D}}
\in R_D(m_D).
\]
Thus the chosen \(\mathbf M^0\) witnesses \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\).  The first implication in the displayed hierarchy is \(\mathrm{lem:structural\text{-}separation\text{-}implies\text{-}active\text{-}slice}\), and composing it with the implication just proved gives the stated hierarchy.

For strictness of the second implication, take a binary DAG with two root vertices feeding a third vertex and no bidirected edges.  Every district is therefore a singleton.  Let \(D\) be the district of the first root.  In a target-domain baseline, let the second root be a fair Bernoulli variable, let the two roots be independent, and let the third vertex be the deterministic indicator that the roots are equal.  Supply only the complete marginal law of the third vertex, which is Bernoulli with success probability \(1/2\).  The observed alphabets are the original binary alphabets.

For the focal root, \(\Omega_D=\{0,1\}\).  The supplied marginal cell is cross-district, so \(\mathrm{def:stacked\text{-}menu\text{-}system}\) retains no raw district-local row; and the marginal law of the child alone provides neither a context nor a fixing quotient exposing the root, so \(\mathrm{def:typed\text{-}extraction\text{-}judgment}\) supplies no derived focal row.  Hence \(A_D=\mathbf 1^\top\),
\[
\mathcal K_D(m_D)=\Delta(\{0,1\}),\qquad
Z_D(m_D)=\varnothing,\qquad
R_D(m_D)=\operatorname{span}\{(1,1)\}.
\]
Fix the baseline response profile of the third vertex at the stated equality table.  For the supplied success cell, fixing the second root at zero gives the focal slice \((1,0)\), while fixing it at one gives \((0,1)\).  Neither row belongs to \(R_D(m_D)\), so \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) fails.  The baseline nonfocal law assigns probability \(1/2\) to each of these two relevant profiles, and therefore
\[
\bar\chi^{\star,\mathbf M^0}_{\{\text{third vertex}=1\}}
=\tfrac12(1,0)+\tfrac12(0,1)
=\tfrac12(1,1)\in R_D(m_D).
\]
For the failure cell the two slices are interchanged, so its average is also \(\tfrac12(1,1)\).  These are all complete cells of the supplied law.  A singleton district is bidirected complete, and \(\mathrm{def:focal\text{-}district\text{-}saturated\text{-}model\text{-}class}\) permits every law on the focal root response block while the fair second-root law and deterministic child table remain fixed.  Consequently the displayed baseline belongs to \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\) and witnesses \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\).  Thus baseline-averaged separation can hold when active-slice separation fails.

sampling_model.design: Exact population laws from finite source-labelled menus of observational, hard-interventional, and declared realizable partial-copy regimes.
sampling_model.units: Each law is generated by independent units from its domain-specific finite recursive SCM; identification is at the population-law level.
sampling_model.treatment: Treatments and partial-copy operations are fixed by descriptor \(a\), and source shifts are encoded by \(\Delta_s\).
sampling_model.overlap: No blanket positivity assumption is imposed. The recursion returns \(\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE}(F_E,z)\) for an identified zero evidence probability, and arm-order theorems explicitly restrict to a face on which the common evidence row is positive.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance estimator enters the identification claim; finite-sample estimation of returned functionals and dual margins is downstream.

tldr: Heterogeneous sites can supply genuine Layer-3 partial-copy laws. A certified extraction judgment turns each available context and cell into a typed district row only after source admissibility is proved. On a fixed-alphabet one-district compatibility face, the sharp transported arm-gap equals an explicit dual weighting of all retained source-labelled cells, and an added Layer-3 regime block yields a finite piecewise-affine pruning frontier. DCTFTR is an inductive, terminating transition system with typed failures and zero-evidence rejection. A complete binary instance gives the margin \(2p-1/2\), while minimum-cost regime-block acquisition and multi-district face preservation remain explicit open questions.

project_justification.gap: CTFTR transports conditional counterfactuals from heterogeneous Layer-1/2 inputs, CTFIDU+ identifies from Layer-3 inputs in one causal specification, and Park--Lee pruning uses graph-based action classes or fixed transported bounds. None derives an exact source-menu certificate or a sign-regime boundary for the order of conditional Layer-3 arms.
project_justification.niche: District-closed shifts and common-evidence arm comparisons reduce one confounded target block to a boundary-sensitive response polytope. Its LP dual converts released source cells into an auditable ranking certificate, while a candidate menu value parametrizes a genuine pruning phase transition.
project_justification.fill: The project proves fixed-alphabet realization of the compatible face, gives certified typed extraction and an inductive DCTFTR semantics, replaces global row span by an active-face criterion, derives sharp primal--dual arm-order certificates, verifies the complete binary phase boundary, and poses minimum-cost regime-block acquisition before asking whether the construction survives multi-district gluing.

related_work: Correa, Lee, and Bareinboim (2022, Theorem 5.1) supply the source-labelled conditional transport architecture for Layers 1 and 2; Proposition 1 proves proper typed inclusion of their problem-instance subgrammar and sound semantic agreement of successful functionals, without asserting syntactic or transition-level equivalence. Raghavan and Bareinboim (2026, Theorem 3.5 and Appendix E.1) supply Layer-3 factor extraction and ctf-thickets for one causal specification; Proposition 1 embeds that setting through \(\mathcal S=\{\star\}\) and proves non-representability of the complete binary multi-domain instance, without claiming that its scalar cell alone is outside CTFIDU+. Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim (2022, Theorem 2.4) supply the finite response carrier, and Choe et al. (2026, Proposition 3.1) motivate preserving all information rows; both inform rather than serve as tightening targets. Bareinboim and Pearl (2012, Theorems 5--7) and Bareinboim and Pearl (2014) supply vertex-level selection diagrams and multi-environment completeness, whereas district joint-kernel invariance is a stronger Layer-3 transport condition. Park and Lee (2026, ICLR, Theorems 1--3) define realizable Layer-3 action classes, and Park and Lee (2026, UAI, Theorems 1--2) give valid Layer-1/2 transported bandit bounds; they inform the menu-dual order certificate, binary pruning boundary, and ex-post block-acquisition question rather than serving as results claimed to be beaten.
technical_internal_limitation: Boundary fibers require the active normals \(e_\omega\) for \(\omega\in Z_D(m_D)\); ordinary row span alone can miss identification when the menu forces response profiles to zero. Multi-district completeness is not asserted. The smallest binary two-hedge thicket must compare every recursive failure with target-score constancy on the exact global compatibility fiber; a failed recursion with a constant target would redirect the global claim to sharp polynomial transported bounds.
honest_scope: The face projection, active-face identification criterion, dual arm-order theorem, one-cell phase diagram, and complete binary check concern a reduced one-district comparison with common positive evidence. DCTFTR soundness covers broader district-closed instances, but fixed-cardinality multi-district completeness is open. The acquisition objective is finite and ex post; it is not an ex-ante adaptive policy. No assumption supplies the dominance margin, active face, or threshold. The observational and hard-interventional problem-instance subgrammar is properly included in DCTFTR and successful outputs agree semantically with the target, the one-domain problem-instance class includes the CTFIDU+ setting, and sure evidence reduces conditional arm order to the unconditional numerator-gap program.
